summary: All 22 units were re-read in full from the fresh packets and every numeric, MCQ and localisation key was worked independently; no wrong keys, unsafe guidance or major factual errors were found. The round-1 major (face-orbit-neck q010) is fixed: the marking guide now says posterior-triangle accessory nerve injury weakens trapezius only, consistent with the hook and explanation. The three round-1 minor precision issues that were not edited (AHI band overlap, the pons worked example attributing isolated lateral rectus palsy to the abducens nucleus, and the jaw-referral explanation) remain, together with the incomplete internal-capsule blood supply statement; all are minor. This is an AI review only: the course still needs a subject-matter expert before clinical reliance.

issues.problem: Lesson states AHI severity as "mild at 5-15, moderate at 15-30 and severe above 30 events per hour". The bands overlap at 15 and 30 and the normal range (<5) is not given. The keyed question (AHI 24) is unaffected.
issues.suggestedFix: State the bands as normal <5, mild 5 to <15, moderate 15 to 30, severe >30 events per hour.

issues.problem: Pons worked example says "The abducens nucleus and facial nerve fascicle lie in the caudal pontine tegmentum, so damage causes ipsilateral eye abduction failure". A nuclear abducens lesion produces an ipsilateral horizontal gaze palsy, not an isolated lateral rectus palsy; the isolated abduction failure with facial weakness and contralateral hemiparesis (Millard-Gubler) is a fascicular lesion in the ventral pons.
issues.suggestedFix: Say the abducens and facial nerve fascicles (not the abducens nucleus) are damaged as they traverse the ventral caudal pons, name the pattern as Millard-Gubler, and optionally note that a nuclear lesion gives gaze palsy.

issues.problem: Explanation says cardiac afferents "enter the upper thoracic cord and converge on the same neurones that receive input from the arm" and so the pain is referred "to the arm and jaw". T1-T4 convergence explains the arm and chest; jaw referral is attributed to convergence of vagal and cervical afferents with trigeminal input in the brainstem and upper cervical cord.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep option a as the key. Amend the explanation so the arm is explained by T1-T4 convergence and the jaw by brainstem/upper cervical convergence.

issues.problem: Lesson and explanation attribute internal capsule supply to MCA lenticulostriate branches only. The posterior limb also receives supply from the anterior choroidal artery (ICA branch) and the anterior limb from the recurrent artery of Heubner (ACA). The key remains the only defensible option.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one sentence noting the anterior choroidal artery supplies the posterior limb of the internal capsule, and that lacunes arise from small penetrating arteries generally.
